clue.text: Colour blue round lips

indicators.note: the word for a Tory goes round the other piece, enclosing it

parts.note: blue is the Conservative party colour, so blue gives CON, short for Conservative
lips are rims, as of a cup or crater

explanation.surface: A make-up note: a shade of blue painted around someone's lips.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Blue' looks like a colour beside the definition 'Colour', but it is the political sense: blue means Conservative in Britain.
explanation.definitionFit: A deep red shade is one particular colour, so the hyponym fits the general word.

clue.text: Image over an awning

indicators.note: the image word sits over and around the other piece, covering it

parts.note: an image is a copy or likeness

explanation.surface: A picture placed over an awning.
explanation.definitionFit: A cloth cover stretched overhead for shade is a synonym for an awning.

clue.text: Claiming victory, still upset

indicators.note: claiming means taking hold of, so the word for still takes the victory letter inside it

parts.note: inert means still, motionless

explanation.surface: Someone claiming victory yet still upset about it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'upset' is a verb here, to overturn, not an adjective meaning distressed.
explanation.definitionFit: To upset an object is to turn it over, which is to turn it upside down.

clue.text: An aid to pronunciation, that's the way to comment about ship

parts.note: ST, short for street, is a way

indicators.note: the comment word goes about the ship, enclosing it

parts.note: a remark is a comment
SS stands for steamship

explanation.surface: Advice that the right way to talk about a ship is with a particular pronunciation.
explanation.definitionFit: An accent sign showing which syllable is emphasised helps a reader say a word correctly.

clue.text: One identifying someone on camera from the swagger, by all conclusions

indicators.note: the conclusions of all the words are their final letters, taken in order

explanation.surface: A witness picking out a swaggering suspect from camera footage.
explanation.walkthrough: 'by all conclusions' takes the last letters of 'on camera from the swagger'.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who identifies a person by stating who they are is one who names them.

clue.text: A trodden-on jellyfish?

parts.note: a jellyfish, having no backbone, is a spineless person, and one who is walked over is a pushover laid at the threshold

explanation.walkthrough: The surface pictures a squashed sea creature; the real reading is a spineless (jellyfish) person who lets everyone walk over them.
explanation.definitionFit: A submissive person whom others exploit is figuratively a mat at the door that everyone wipes their feet on.

clue.text: Shame to stop drinking purest fluid

indicators.note: drinking means taking in, so the word for stopping swallows the other letters

parts.note: to die is to stop, as an engine dies

indicators.note: fluid means flowing and changeable, so the letters of purest are rearranged

explanation.surface: A temperance message: the shame of drinking should stop, even of pure spirit.
explanation.walkthrough: 'drinking' looks like the subject of the surface, but it is the container signal: 'to stop' (to die) takes in the letters of 'purest' made 'fluid', just after its first two letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Being held in disrepute means being in low public regard, a state of disgrace.

clue.text: Neither knife nor fork cut up — oh dear!

indicators.note: in a down clue, up means the letters read from bottom to top, backwards
cut means docked, losing its final letter

parts.note: the remaining item of cutlery is a spoon

explanation.surface: Someone dropping cutlery: not the knife, not the fork, oh dear!
explanation.walkthrough: 'cut' docks SPOON to SPOO, and 'up' turns it round.
explanation.definitionFit: An exclamation of mild dismay at a small blunder is an interjection like oh dear.

clue.text: Court feature in wonderful drawing?

indicators.note: the court feature is placed in the wonderful word

parts.note: magic is informal for wonderful
a tennis court has a net across it

explanation.surface: A tennis court featured in a wonderful sketch.
explanation.walkthrough: 'drawing' looks like a picture but means pulling towards, as a magnet does.
explanation.definitionFit: Something attracting or pulling things towards it, as a lodestone does iron, is described this way.

clue.text: Policeman supports judge in meeting

indicators.note: in a down clue the supporting piece sits beneath the other

parts.note: to try a case is to judge it
Sting was singer of the band The Police, so a Police man

explanation.surface: A police officer backing a judge in a meeting.
explanation.definitionFit: A lovers' secret rendezvous is a tryst, so the -ing form names such a meeting.

clue.text: Struggling after heavy meal? Nice? No! Turn to dietary wisdom from …

indicators.note: struggling suggests letters thrashing about, so the following words are to be rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone groaning after a big dinner on the Riviera turns to dieting advice.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Struggling' signals rearranging all of 'after heavy meal Nice No Turn to'; the ellipsis carries on into the next clue, naming the speaker as the Muppets pig.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase is a comic piece of diet advice attributed to the Muppets' porcine diva, so it is her dietary wisdom.

clue.text: … Fleming role: is Bond possibly scoffing one horse, the greedy one?

parts.note: M is the spymaster in Ian Fleming's Bond novels

indicators.note: scoffing means eating up, so the spy word swallows the other letters

parts.note: James Bond is an example of a spy
one is the Roman numeral I
GG, short for gee-gee, is a child's word for a horse

explanation.surface: Continuing from the previous clue: a Fleming character wondering if Bond is eating a whole horse.
explanation.walkthrough: The clue follows on from 9 with an ellipsis: this character is the source of that dietary wisdom.
explanation.definitionFit: The Muppets' glamorous pig is famously gluttonous, so she is the greedy one of the show.

clue.text: Kidnapper, inexperienced poisoner

parts.note: Paris of Troy carried off Helen, the abduction that started the Trojan War
green means inexperienced, a novice

explanation.surface: A novice abductor who turns out to be a poisoner as well.
explanation.definitionFit: This emerald pigment is an arsenic compound once used as a rat poison and insecticide, so it poisons.

clue.text: Socialist walked out

definitions.meaning: in politics the socialist wing sits on this side, the opposite of right
past tense of leave: departed, walked away

explanation.surface: A socialist storming out of a meeting.
explanation.definitionFit: The political wing on the socialist side shares spelling with the past tense of leave, meaning departed.

clue.text: Barber's work, Adagio for Strings, by all conclusions suits Christmas concert initially, when jazzed up

indicators.note: jazzing up livens and reworks something, so the collected letters are rearranged
the final letters of each of the three words are taken
initially means the first letter of each word

explanation.surface: A programme note: Barber's Adagio for Strings suits a Christmas concert when given a jazz treatment.
explanation.walkthrough: Samuel Barber wrote Adagio for Strings, a famous piece; here 'Barber's work' is a haircut. The pool is ORS + SUITS + CC.
explanation.definitionFit: A haircut made with shears rather than clippers is the work of a hairdresser, a barber.

clue.text: See 17
One perhaps requiring fresh hint with clue about possum's bottom

indicators.note: the rearranged letters go about the single letter, enclosing it
fresh means new, so the letters are made afresh in a new order
a word's bottom is its last letter

explanation.surface: A solver needing a new hint for a clue about a possum's rear end.
explanation.walkthrough: 'One' is the time of day, one o'clock; 'possum's bottom' gives M, set among the reworked HINT and CLUE.
explanation.definitionFit: One o'clock is a typical midday meal hour, so it is an example of the meal break.

clue.text: Crook with rash deeds in store, perhaps?

parts.note: a crook is a bend or curve, an arc
hives is an itchy skin rash

explanation.surface: A criminal with reckless deeds kept in storage.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Crook' is a bend, not a criminal, and 'rash' is the skin complaint, not reckless.
explanation.definitionFit: Collections of historical records, such as property deeds kept in storage, are a record office's holdings.

clue.text: Action blamed for embarrassingly affected manner, as boob revealed on the catwalk?

definitions.text: as boob revealed on the catwalk?

parts.note: war is military action

indicators.note: embarrassingly suggests things in awkward disarray, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: unction is an affected, oily earnestness of manner

explanation.surface: A model blamed for an embarrassing mishap, flashing a breast on the catwalk.
explanation.walkthrough: 'boob' doubles as a blunder and a breast; 'embarrassingly' reworks BLAMED FOR into DROBEMALF.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase was coined for a costume failure exposing a performer on stage, as a breast might be shown during a fashion show.

clue.text: Birds, by the sound of it, travelled on skis

indicators.note: the phrase tells us the past-tense word is heard, and spelt as a word that sounds the same

parts.note: rode means travelled on horseback or by vehicle
skis, like sled blades, are runners

explanation.surface: Somebody who got about on skis, as reported by others.
explanation.definitionFit: These are fast-running cuckoos of the American south-west, so they are birds.

clue.text: Engine not starting, tank fills up — might this be the size of the issue?

indicators.note: the tank fills the shortened engine word, going inside it
not starting means losing the first letter

parts.note: a loco, short for locomotive, is a railway engine

indicators.note: in a down clue up means read from the bottom, backwards

parts.note: a vat is a large tank

explanation.surface: A car's engine won't start though the tank is full: is that the issue?
explanation.walkthrough: 'issue' is a publication, not a problem: an octavo is a book size. A loco is a railway engine; in a down clue 'up' turns the tank word, and 'not starting' drops the engine's first letter.
explanation.definitionFit: A book format made by folding each printed sheet into eight leaves describes the size of a publication.

clue.text: Tense figure, old magistrate with nothing to lose

parts.note: one is a number, a figure

indicators.note: nothing is the letter O, which the magistrate word must lose

parts.note: the doge was the elected chief magistrate of old Venice and Genoa

explanation.surface: A nervous former magistrate who has nothing left to lose.
explanation.definitionFit: Being nervous and jumpy is the idiom for feeling tense and edgy.

clue.text: Papers stuffed inside gas mask

indicators.note: the papers are stuffed inside the gas symbol, so it encloses them

parts.note: HE is the chemical symbol for helium, a gas
papers are identity documents, ID

explanation.surface: Documents stuffed into a gas mask, perhaps for smuggling.
explanation.walkthrough: 'gas mask' reads as one object, but 'gas' is wordplay and 'mask' alone is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: To mask something is to conceal or cover it, a synonym of the verb.

clue.text: See 9
Explosive ingredient added to biriani, treacherous

indicators.note: the letters are added into the run of words, sitting inside them across the gap

explanation.surface: Something explosive has been slipped into a curry, treacherously.
explanation.definitionFit: Saltpetre, potassium nitrate, is a component of gunpowder, so an ingredient of an explosive.

clue.text: See 9
Musician I love nothing about coming into view, shortly

indicators.note: the group of letters comes into the shortened view word, entering it
shortly means cut short, losing its last letter

parts.note: a vista is a view
love is zero in tennis, the letter O

indicators.note: about means turned round, so the word for nothing is read backwards

parts.note: nil means nothing

explanation.surface: A musician saying they adore nothing about appearing on stage.
explanation.walkthrough: 'love' is zero in tennis scoring, the letter O. 'about' turns the word for nothing round, and 'shortly' cuts the view word's last letter; the group goes in just after its first letter.
explanation.definitionFit: A fiddler is a player of a stringed instrument, a type of musician.

clue.text: Cold, frozen vegetable

parts.note: C is the abbreviation for cold, as on taps
frozen means solid, hard

explanation.surface: A cold, frozen vegetable, straight from the freezer.
explanation.definitionFit: Swiss chard is a leafy green beet grown for its leaves and stalks, a vegetable.

clue.text: Enclose PM in silence, having dropped guts

indicators.note: the prime minister goes inside what is left of the silence word
dropping the guts means losing all the inside letters, keeping the outer pair

parts.note: Edward Heath was British Prime Minister 1970 to 1974

explanation.surface: A prime minister being contained by a gagging order after losing his nerve.
explanation.walkthrough: 'having dropped guts' leaves only S and E of 'silence'. Edward Heath was a British Conservative prime minister.
explanation.definitionFit: To put a blade into its scabbard is to encase or enclose it.

clue.text: See 9
